flashcards.q: Key cost levers on the Gemini API?
flashcards.a: Context caching (reduced rates on repeated prefixes, TTL-billed), batch mode ~50% off for async work (~), thinking budgets capping reasoning tokens, tiered input pricing above ~200K tokens (~), and routing simple paths to Flash-class models.

flashcards.q: What are the operational limits of 1M-token context?
flashcards.a: First-token latency at ~500K tokens runs 30-90s (~) - not real-time; needle-recall stays high but complex multi-hop reasoning degrades across the span (context rot); quality is not uniform from edge to middle (lost-in-the-middle).

Code-first: Agent(name, model, instruction, tools) as the unit; workflow agents (sequential/parallel/loop) give deterministic structure around LLM agents; tools are Python functions/OpenAPI specs/built-ins; multi-agent trees delegate; evaluations are testable artifacts. Open source, Python/TS/Go/Java/Kotlin, model-agnostic.

flashcards.q: What does Agent Engine buy vs ADK on Cloud Run?
flashcards.a: Managed runtime: session/state persistence without your datastore, Memory Bank cross-session recall, auth wiring to Vertex endpoints, eval hooks. Cost: platform pricing + lock-in. Self-hosting on Cloud Run/GKE keeps portability - you own checkpointing.

Brute-force = exact at small scale. Tree-AH: batch-built, high-QPS approximate serving, updates via rebuild cadence. Streaming-friendly types support incremental upserts with propagation lag (~). Filtering executes pre-filter during search via namespaces - preserves recall vs post-filtering.

flashcards.q: When is Vector Search the wrong choice?
flashcards.a: Below roughly 10M vectors (~): pgvector/AlloyDB AI or BigQuery vector types serve smaller corpora with less infra. The ANN platform earns its keep at billion-scale and heavy QPS.

RAG: repeated queries against shared/stable corpora, frequently-changing data, citation requirements - cost per query stays small. Long context: one-shot holistic analysis of static documents, no retrieval infra. Re-sent context costs linearly per query; caches discount but expire.

flashcards.q: What does Model Garden actually provide operationally?
flashcards.a: 200+ models (Google + third-party like Claude) behind one IAM/quota/network boundary - enables capability routing and provider swaps without new security reviews. Caveats: schema/rate-limit/error semantics differ subtly per provider behind the surface.

flashcards.q: Why might context caching not reduce costs?
flashcards.a: Cache storage bills while alive and pays off only above hit-rate thresholds; unique prefixes (per-user personalization baked into system prompts) never hit. Fix structure: volatile content in message tail, static knowledge in cached prefix.

flashcards.q: How should agent identities be governed on GCP?
flashcards.a: Dedicated service identity per agent, least-privilege roles scoped to its tools, PAB caps on reachable resources, audit attribution per tool call, org policy banning keys (auth via attached SA/WIF). Prevents prompt injection becoming privilege escalation via borrowed human credentials.

flashcards.q: Version discipline for production Gemini usage?
flashcards.a: Pin explicit model version identifiers instead of -latest aliases (aliases move behavior overnight); run staging canaries against new versions before switching; keep golden-set evals as CI gates on prompt/model/tool changes.

flashcards.q: vLLM-on-GKE vs Gemini API decision criteria?
flashcards.a: Self-host when: data residency bars external processing, custom/open weights only, steady volume amortizes GPU pools, deep serving control needed. API when frontier capability required, traffic spiky (idle GPUs bleed money), ops scarce. Sustained utilization above ~half GPU capacity favors owning (~).
